answer: One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity bonded to a slow, expensive resource. Each agent locks a basalt-grade bond on-chain; new identities must wait through a cooling epoch before voting. A sybil farm would need to fund thousands of bonds, each a hollow shell until it holds real value, and every extra identity multiplies that cost. Reputation then accrues only through verified work, so a whisper of a fake cluster never gains quorum weight. Attack cost scales linearly with identities, making mass forgery economically irrational.
